_doc: The comms law: who gets answered how fast, per thread class (ported in shape from the property OS's scripts/comms/law.json, 2026-10-06). Read by comms_state.py (SLA + state) and the operator prompt. Hours are wall-clock. A class is picked by the thread's lane and the party: a number or address that came through the Package Finder quiz or a HoneyBook lead is a lead; a booked couple is a couple; owner's lane is her own; everything else is personal (recorded, triaged, never auto-drafted).

lead._why: Speed wins on quiz leads (the owner 2026-10-05): a text within 15 minutes, a card to the owner within 5.

personal._why: the owner (2026-10-06): every personal text gets a reply card in his voice, with the thread as context, so he only taps Send / Edit & send in Chat. Noise (codes, marketing, tapbacks, the example-SEND nudge) is still dropped.

hard_rails: Nothing reaches a client, vendor or anyone outside the household without an owner's tap on a card showing the exact words and recipient.
No price, discount, delivery date or turnaround is promised to a couple without an owner's approval.
A text is under 320 characters, first names, one question back, no greeting line, no sign-off.
A draft is not a send: a thread is 'awaiting them' only after the phone acked the send or Sent mail shows it.
Verification codes, short-code and automated texts, marketing, reactions: closed, never drafted.

wake._burst: 3+ texts waiting and the newest under 8 min old = a group chat still moving: hold the wake until it settles (the owner 2026-10-07)
